description: An erect annual herb 30-60 cm tall with trifoliate leaves, small pale yellow-white pea-like flowers and long, slender, beaked pods holding 10-20 hard, angular, golden-brown seeds.
cultural_significance: Leaves (methi) and seeds are a staple of Indian kitchens and tempering (tadka). Seeds are given to new mothers in traditional diets, such as methi laddoo in Maharashtra and Gujarat.
habitat: Cool to mild climates with well-drained loam; grown as a winter crop in India and across the Mediterranean region.

uses.title: Prameha (diabetes-like conditions)
uses.detail: Soaked seeds taken in the morning are traditionally used in Prameha; clinical studies suggest modest blood-sugar benefits.

uses.title: Digestion and appetite
uses.detail: Seeds and leaves are described as Deepana; used for loss of appetite, bloating and dysentery.

uses.title: Postnatal care and lactation
uses.detail: Seeds are traditionally given to new mothers to support milk flow and recovery; evidence is limited.

uses.title: Hair care
uses.detail: Soaked seed paste is applied to the scalp to condition hair and reduce dandruff.

uses.title: Cholesterol and blood sugar research
uses.detail: Fenugreek fibre and saponins have been studied for lowering cholesterol and glucose.

preparations.name: Methika beeja (soaked seeds)
preparations.method: Soak a small amount of seeds in water overnight and consume with the water.
preparations.note: Traditional morning use for blood sugar and digestion.

preparations.name: Methika churna
preparations.method: Dry roast the seeds lightly and grind to powder.

preparations.name: Methi laddoo
preparations.method: Seeds roasted and mixed with jaggery, ghee and nuts.
preparations.note: Postnatal winter food in western India.

preparations.name: Hair paste
preparations.method: Grind soaked seeds into a paste and apply to the scalp.

precautions: May lower blood sugar; people on diabetes medicines should monitor closely. Avoid medicinal quantities in pregnancy, as it may stimulate the uterus. May cause gas and loose motions, and may cause a maple-syrup smell in sweat and urine. Possible allergy in people sensitive to legumes (chickpea, peanut). Use caution with anticoagulants.

cultivation.propagation: Direct sowing of seeds in autumn
cultivation.harvest: Cut leaves in 3-4 weeks; harvest pods when yellow, about 3-4 months

fun_fact: Fenugreek is one of the oldest cultivated medicinal plants; seeds were found in Tutankhamun's tomb, and the name 'foenum-graecum' means 'Greek hay'.

regions.name: South Asia (Widely cultivated)
regions.note: Winter crop in kitchens and fields
